fn extrude_interval(profile: &[Curve], arrangement: &Arrangement, base: Vector3, tip: Vector3, taper: f64) -> Outcome<Solid> — internal generalized form (D1): bottom cap on z=base.z, top cap on z=tip.z; Line edges sweep to canonical Planes in any sweep direction; Circle edges -> canonical Cylinder (z-parallel sweep, taper==0) or canonical z-aligned Cone (taper!=0, apex on the axis from bottom r at z0 and top r' at z1); oblique sweep of a circle edge -> UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier); no Placed carriers emitted

fn offset_profile_for_taper + re-arrange (D4): the top profile is the signed 2-D offset (outer lines toward material by d along the CCW left normal, hole lines away from the hole interior, both endpoints extended by 2|d|; outer circles r-d, hole circles r+d; r-d<=0 or r+d<=0 -> Collapsed(ApexVanishing)) re-arranged through the landed arrange; cycle roles by containment (never winding sign); carrier-identity edge pairing, cycle-count + cyclic carrier-order checks and a material-side representative check refuse Collapsed(KnifeEdge) on any top-region topology event (inverted inset, split carrier, structure mismatch, arrange refusal of the offset)

deviations: Downward vector sweeps are normalized by swapping base/tip inside extrude_interval. Derivation: D2 permits dir.z<0 ('both == false -> interval [0, dir]' does not exclude negative dir), but the landed cap/side orientation conventions (bottom cap inverted, sides stored uninverted on Plane(a, b, a+sweep-top)) assume an upward sweep; for a downward sweep the plane's natural normal flips and the emitted faces would point inward. The swap preserves the solid's point set exactly ({base + t*(tip-base)} is invariant), so downward extrusion yields the same correct outward-oriented solid.

extrude_profile_vector refuses non-finite dir with Refusal::Empty (D2 specifies only dir.z==0). Derivation: the landed entry refuses non-finite height (the extrude.rs convention D2 explicitly invokes); an infinite sweep is the same empty-domain case. The interval additionally gates sweep.z finiteness.

Test 10 (negative_taper_expands_material) uses a 6x6 base rectangle rather than the 4x4 fixture of tests 5/7. Derivation: with d=0.5 the 4x4 0.5-outset puts each miter-corner crossing parameter at 0.5/6 = 1/12, which the landed S1 arrange refuses - ratio_to_f64 (arrange.rs) requires the reduced crossing parameter to be a dyadic rational, so line_line_intersection returns NumericallyUnresolved(RootNotIsolated), which the D4 handling maps to Collapsed. (The 4x4 0.5-INSET of test 5 dodges this: its parameters are 3/4 and 1/4.) The 6x6 outset puts the parameters at {1/16, 15/16} (dyadic) and the test verifies exactly the specified semantics: negative taper expands the material, the top cap is the 0.5-outset rectangle, Solid::try_new ok. The landed arrange is outside this packet's write_allow, so the domain restriction is recorded rather than widened.

Test 8 (taper_hole_grows) uses hole radius r=0.75 with d=0.5; the packet fixed neither r nor tan(taper). Derivation: with the 4x4 plate's r=1.0 and d=0.5, the grown top circle (r+d=1.5) is exactly TANGENT to the 0.5-inset boundary lines (distance from (2,2) to each inset line is 1.5) - a degenerate double-root topology event. r=0.75 keeps the offset re-arrangement exact (grown radius 1.25, clearance 0.25) and the test verifies the specified semantics: 2 top-cap wires, the hole's top radius r+d, Solid::try_new ok.

Refusal::Collapsed payloads are KnifeEdge for offset topology events (arrange refusal of the offset profile, top-region structure/order/side-check events, pairing degeneracies) and ApexVanishing for vanished circle radii (r-d<=0 outer, r+d<=0 hole). Derivation: the packet writes Collapsed(..) without fixing the payload; both CollapseReason arms pre-existed (zero-new-arms respected). KnifeEdge matches the lfs->0 reading of a region collapsing; ApexVanishing is literally the 16.1 apex-vanishing of the tapered wall cone.

All emitted solids keep the landed certificate shape with method: Method::Exact, including cone-bearing tapers, although Cone::new internally certifies its own carrier as Method::Float. Derivation: D5 specifies the acceptance gates (Solid::try_new + carrier recognition) and is silent on the method field; the frozen landed certificate was preserved verbatim rather than inventing a per-carrier method split the packet did not book.
